selectedOriginals.inspection: Full selected2006west street view individually inspected: two square stages and tall open octagonal lantern, pale stone tracery/quoins against warmer masonry, square green skeletal clock frame/gold ring/hands before central open pointed window. Lower tower paired stacked blind-niche stages/central larger arches, long triple-panel second-stage face, pierced Gothic gallery parapets, short slate/lead pyramidal roof and cross/gold vane. Shops/wires excluded.

selectedOriginals.caption: Panorama Utrecht met Dom en Buurkerk
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full selected2008panorama individually inspected. DomTower is taller slender background tower; large foreground square tower belongs toBuurkerk, not this asset. Cathedral choir and neighborhood also excluded. Retains detached three-stage skyline/short octagonal cap, no cathedral nave duplicate.

additionalInspected.caption: Dom cathedral tower seen from the Stadhuisbrug in Utrecht
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2008NWoblique individually inspected. Five-bay lower square face with larger center pointed window and blind brick flanks, three bays at narrower second square: real open center with two mullions/louvers below clock, flanks blind. Repeated pierced pointed/trefoil gallery rails and crocketed pinnacles, octagonal upper lantern with divided giant windows/open tracery, two horizontal light bands and buttressed corners. Eight short gables ring low roof/green upper railing.

additionalInspected.caption: The Dom Tower in Utrecht, the Netherlands is one of the best known landmarks of this country. This gothic tower is the highest church tower (112,5 metres/368 feet) in the Netherlands and was built between 1321 and 1382 as part of the Cathedral of St. Martin. The resolution of the original photograph is 7768*4150.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2009day elevated original individually inspected from localUtrecht collection. Strong control on two square/one octagonal proportions, warm brick/stone pale quoins and blind twin-lancet tracery versus real openings. Lower front central glazed pointed window with balcony above deep portal; clocks four sides/green square corner circles/gold rings. Upper lantern visibly open through paired light sections and horizontal stone band. Neighboring choir/foreground roofs excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: Utrechtse Domtoren bij nacht, gefotografeerd vanuit het noordoosten.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2012NE night original individually inspected. Opposite faces confirm three central/flanking pointed second-stage pattern and low-stage stacked blind niches. Giant octagonal lantern windows are open with physical mullions/horizontal ties. Colored illumination/tree occlusion is not baked into materials.

additionalInspected.caption: Een balkon van de Domtoren.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2009gallery detail individually inspected: real narrow stone walkway, pierced shaped balustrade posts and iron safety mesh/rails; heavy molded stone reveals and inner tower wall. Gallery kept open; no solid painted imitation. Mesh simplified at model scale.

additionalInspected.caption: Domtoren: detail
additionalInspected.inspection: Full1958RCE lantern detail individually inspected as historical construction reference, corroborated by2008/2009/2024images: thick deeply molded pointed opening, two physical main mullions/three lights, horizontal iron ties, central stone tracery band, tall open interior. No claim every1958fastener survives2024; detailed bell machinery excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: Domtoren: detail
additionalInspected.inspection: Full1958RCE pinnacle/roof detail individually inspected as historical construction reference, corroborated in later overall photographs: molded octagonal finials/leaf crochets, stone gabled profile and slate/lead roof seams. Original simplified geometric crochets/gargoyle silhouettes replace fine carvings.
